study_identification.title: Individual deviations from normative models of brain structure in a large cross-sectional schizophrenia cohort

study_characteristics.study_objective: Map individual deviations from normative ranges of cortical thickness and fractional anisotropy in schizophrenia, and test whether deviation loci recapitulate group-average pathology maps; assess associations with polygenic risk and symptoms.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Two-sample t-tests with permutation and FDR across regions/tracts for case–control differences (age/sex controlled); Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) relating regional deviation scores to polygenic risk score and to latent symptom/cognitive dimensions; additional groupwise comparisons of deviation-defined subgroups.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Schizophrenia shows widespread group-level FA/CT reductions, yet individual deviation loci are highly heterogeneous; 79% of patients have one or more infra-normal deviations; higher PRS associates with more infra-normal CT regions.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Compared to healthy controls, the schizophrenia group showed widespread FA and CT reductions across virtually all tracts/regions, but no more than 15–20% of patients deviated at any single locus. 79% of patients exhibited at least one infra-normal deviation (healthy: 59 ± 2%, p < 0.001). Polygenic risk for schizophrenia correlated with the number of CT regions with infra-normal deviations (r = -0.17, p = 0.006), especially in frontal/temporal cortices.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Potential measurement noise and artifacts despite QC; dMRI acquired on 1.5T single-shell limiting microstructural specificity; diffusion harmonization not reproduced for two smallest sites; subjective normative thresholds (5–95%); possible confounding from medication, onset age, illness duration.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Individual deviation maps may facilitate personalized interventions, target selection for neuromodulation, and stratification into subgroups; normative modeling aids parsing heterogeneity.

general_notes.general_notes: Five Australian sites (Brisbane, Sydney, Melbourne, Perth, Newcastle); identical scanner model (Siemens Avanto) and sequences across sites; diffusion harmonization used rotation invariant spherical harmonics mapping to Brisbane reference; FA normalized with ANTs to standard space; atlas choices: ICBM-DTI-81 (WM), Desikan–Killiany (cortex).
